questions.stem: A ray of light hits a plane mirror at an angle of 35° to the mirror surface. What is the angle of reflection?
questions.explanation: Angles of incidence and reflection are measured from the normal (perpendicular to the surface), not from the surface itself. If the ray hits at 35° to the surface, the angle of incidence is 90° - 35° = 55° from the normal. By the law of reflection, the angle of reflection also equals 55°. Option A (35°) is a very common mistake — students often measure from the surface rather than the normal.

questions.stem: A person stands 2 m in front of a plane mirror. How far does their image appear to be from them?
questions.explanation: In a plane mirror, the image forms the same distance behind the mirror as the object is in front. So the image is 2 m behind the mirror. The total distance from the person to their image is 2 m + 2 m = 4 m. Option B (2 m) is the distance from the person to the mirror, not to the image.

questions.stem: An echo is heard 0.6 seconds after a person shouts towards a cliff. If the speed of sound is 340 m/s, how far away is the cliff?
questions.explanation: The sound travels to the cliff and back, so the total distance is d = v x t = 340 x 0.6 = 204 m. Since this is the round trip, the cliff distance = 204 / 2 = 102 m. Option A (204 m) is a common error — forgetting that the sound has to travel there AND back. Always halve the total distance for echo calculations.

questions.stem: Which property of the image formed in a plane mirror makes it different from the actual object?

options.text: The image is smaller than the object
The image is laterally inverted (left and right are swapped)
The image is a different colour

questions.explanation: Images in plane mirrors are laterally inverted — left and right appear swapped. This is why ambulances have 'AMBULANCE' written in mirror writing on the front. The image is the same size (not smaller, option A), upright not inverted (option B), and the same colour (option D). The image is also virtual, meaning it cannot be projected onto a screen.

questions.stem: A concert hall uses curved reflective panels on the walls and ceiling. What is the purpose of these panels?

options.text: To increase the speed of sound in the hall
To change the frequency of the sound waves
To direct reflected sound waves towards the audience for even sound distribution
To absorb unwanted sound and prevent echoes

questions.explanation: Curved reflective panels use the law of reflection to direct sound waves towards the audience, ensuring everyone hears the performance clearly. They reflect (not absorb, option D) sound. Reflection does not change the speed (option A) or frequency (option B) of sound — it only changes the direction of the wave.
